newsitem.title: USA: CBOT says meeting with CFTC on deregulation.
newsitem.headline: CBOT says meeting with CFTC on deregulation.

text.p: Attorneys of Chicago Board of Trade are meeting every other week with staff of Commodity Futures Trading Commission to work out a compromise to proposed legislation that would eliminate much of the CFTC's regulatory powers.
"We're meeting about every other week," CBOT President Tom Donovan told Reuters Tuesday. "It's their lawyers meeting with our lawyers at this point."
Donovan spoke after testifying before a House Agriculture subcommittee that is considering a bill to change the CFTC's oversight authority.
"The talks are well worth continuing," he added, declining to elaborate.

In earlier testimony, Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips and Richard Lindsey of Securities and Exchange Commission each said they hoped CFTC could work out a compromise with the big U.S. futures exchanges.
"There's great room for dialogue between the exchanges and the CFTC," said Lindsey, the director of market regulation for the SEC.

CFTC chief Brooksley Born also indicated in her testimony that she supported a move toward less regulation of the futures market, and invited the exchanges to work with her in deregulating the market.
Born has repeatedly said she opposes pending bills in the House and Senate that would eliminate most of the CFTC's regulatory power. ((--Julie Vorman, Washington commodities desk, 202-898-8467))
